A minimal example that proves the scaffold renders and demonstrates the shared
knowledge base + `Underwriter` pattern every post uses. Delete once real
examples exist.

## Problem

Roll three fair dice and sum them. What is the distribution of the total?

## Setup and assumptions

Three independent rolls of a fair six-sided die. As an aggregate: a fixed
frequency of 3 and a discrete uniform severity on `[1:6]`.

## Implementation

Every post starts the same way: an empty `Underwriter`, then load any libraries.
The built-in `build` underwriter loads the `example.agg`, so canonical objects
are available by name. The [SPA](http://agg.mynl.com) also loads `example.agg`.

```{python}
from aggregate import Underwriter, qd

uw = Underwriter(databases=None)     # start empty
uw.load('example')                   # shared assumptions, resolved from project root

a = uw.build('agg ThreeDice dfreq [3] dsev [1:6]')
qd(a)
```

Referencing a built-in object by name, and surfacing its assumptions on the page

```{python}
qd(uw.build('A.ThreeDice'))
```

Look up the object in the `knowledge`.

```{python}
uw.build['A.ThreeDice']
```

## Output

```{python}
a.plot()
```

The mean is 10.5 and the distribution is the familiar triangular-ish hump on
3–18 — the analytic answer, matched exactly.
